chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Dawud, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man died in the era of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who had no inheritor, so Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) handed over his inheritance to his fellow city folk.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits if a person dies with no direct relatives in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* records a specific legal precedent set by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the distribution of *al-mughram* (estate of one without heirs) to the *hamsharih* (fellow city-dwellers or neighbors). It highlights the early application of communal kinship in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing this neighborly claim from other potential heirs like the *aqla* (paternal clan).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from dawood, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A man died in the era of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, not having an inheritor for him, so Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> handed over his inheritance to his fellow city folk’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Dawud from those whom he has mentioned who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
in the time of ’Amir al-Mu’minin a man died and had no heirs. ’Amir al-Mu’minin gave his legacy to his Hamshahrijah (his fellow countryman). 5 ”
